conditions: The event is a "planning session" — some kind of planning-type meeting.
Its scheduled end time is 5:00 PM.
That end time falls on Thursday, 2018-06-21 (the coming Thursday relative to Sunday 2018-06-17).
Its description field contains a mention of "the Q4 roadmap."
Action: set/change the event's location to "Room 2B."

readings: 5:00 PM in America/Los_Angeles (the requester's local timezone)
5:00 PM in whatever timezone the event record itself is stored/displayed in, if different
The event's title/name literally contains "planning session" or a close variant
Any meeting that is substantively a planning-type meeting, identified by content rather than title wording
The literal phrase "Q4 roadmap" appears in the description
The description substantively references Q4 planning/roadmap topics without using that exact phrase

records.note: Title "Planning session", description literally says "Walk through the Q4 roadmap and owners", ends 17:00 (5pm) Pacific on Thursday 2018-06-21. Meets all five conditions.
This event starts at 5pm and ends at 6pm, not ends at 5pm as required. Not a plausible alternate reading of "ends at 5pm."
Ends at 5:30pm, not 5:00pm. Close but clearly fails on a careful reading of the end time.

Title "Q4 roadmap planning" is itself about the Q4 roadmap and can be read as a planning-type meeting (r1 passes), and it does end at 5pm Thursday (r2, r3 pass). But the description field, "Agenda to be confirmed," does not mention the Q4 roadmap at all — the request specifically asks about the description, not the title, so this fails r4 on a careful reading.
Title "Planning session" and end time 5pm Thursday match, but the description, "Hiring plan for the autumn," is about hiring, not the Q4 roadmap.

turn2.differences: My r1–r5 conditions match the request as read in Step 1; no substantive difference. r1 was deliberately phrased broadly (\"some kind of planning-type meeting\") to accommodate the title-vs-description ambiguity noted in Step 1, which turned out not to affect the outcome here since the only record it could have swayed (ev_ps_title) fails independently on r4.

ambiguity_effects.explain: On reflection, a careful reader defaults to the requester's own timezone (America/Los_Angeles) absent any contrary signal, so this isn't genuinely unsettled. It's moot here anyway: every event in the dataset is on Jordan Lee's single calendar with timeZone America/Los_Angeles, so both readings pick the same candidates.

A careful reader could genuinely read this as requiring the literal title "planning session" or as describing any planning-type meeting. This affects whether ev_ps_title (titled "Q4 roadmap planning") counts as r1-eligible, but it doesn't change the final match because that record fails r4 (description doesn't mention Q4 roadmap) under either reading.

Could mean the literal phrase "Q4 roadmap" appears, or any substantive reference to Q4 roadmap topics. In this dataset it doesn't matter: the only description that references the Q4 roadmap under either reading (loose or literal) is ev_ps_target's; the other records' descriptions (hiring plan, agenda TBD) don't reference it under any reasonable reading.

turn2.naturalness_note: Reads like an ordinary request someone would send about their own calendar — identifying a meeting by rough time and topic and asking to change its room. Nothing about the phrasing suggests it was artificially constructed.
